blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Feedback is when we tell someone how they are doing. Good feedback is clear, kind and honest. We say the good things — and also the things that can improve.

When we give feedback, we speak softly and we listen carefully. We do not only talk. We listen too.

Coaching is a type of feedback. But a coach is different. A coach does not give the answers. A coach asks questions. The questions help the other person to think and to find their own answer.

items.q: What is feedback?
options: When we tell someone how they are doing
When we write a long report
items.why: "Feedback is when we tell someone how they are doing."

items.q: Good feedback is…
items.why: "Good feedback is clear, kind and honest."

items.q: What does a coach do?
options: A coach only listens and says nothing
A coach asks questions to help the person think
A coach gives all the answers
A coach writes the answers on paper
items.why: "A coach does not give the answers. A coach asks questions."

items.q: The text says we "listen carefully." This suggests that…
options: we should only talk, not listen
listening is not important in feedback
we should listen only to the manager
listening is an important part of good feedback
items.why: Inferência: o texto valoriza ouvir com atenção — ouvir faz parte do bom feedback, não só falar.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with this idea:
options: A good coach gives the person all the answers.
We should be kind when we give feedback.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que um coach NÃO dá respostas; ele faz perguntas. Logo, o autor discordaria disso.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily fazendo coaching com João. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi João, thank you for meeting with me today. Please sit down. I want to talk about your presentation this morning. First, the good news: you did this very well. You spoke clearly and you looked at the people in the room. That was really great.

Now, I am not going to give you all the answers. That is not my job. I want to ask you some questions. So, tell me — how do you think it went? What part was good for you?

Okay, good. And what part can you improve for next time? Take your time. Think slowly. There is no wrong answer here.

Yes, I agree with you. The slides had a lot of words. Next time, try to use fewer words and speak a little more slowly. You work quickly, and that is good, but slow down on the difficult parts. The team needs time to understand.

Remember, I am here to help you think, not to tell you what to do. You already have good ideas. Keep going, João. You are doing very well.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Emily talk about with João?
items.why: "I want to talk about your presentation this morning."

items.q: What good thing did João do?
options: He spoke clearly and looked at the people
items.why: "you spoke clearly and you looked at the people."

items.q: What does Emily ask João to improve?
options: To use more words on the slides
To use fewer words and speak more slowly
items.why: "try to use fewer words and speak a little more slowly."

items.q: Why does Emily ask questions instead of giving answers?
options: Because she does not know the answers
Because she has no time to talk
Because she wants João to think for himself
items.why: Inferência: "I am here to help you think, not to tell you what to do" — ela quer que João pense sozinho.

items.q: How does Emily feel about João's work?
options: She thinks the presentation was very bad
She is angry and wants him to stop
She is bored and does not care
She is positive and wants him to keep going
items.why: Inferência: ela elogia ("you did this very well… Keep going") — o tom é positivo e encorajador.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "She listens carefully before she speaks." Carefully means…
items.why: Carefully = com cuidado/atenção. É um advérbio de modo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Good feedback is clear, ___ and honest."
items.why: "Good feedback is clear, kind and honest." Kind = gentil.

items.q: "A coach asks questions to help you improve." To improve means to…
items.why: To improve = melhorar, ficar melhor.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Please ___ to me before you answer."
items.why: To listen = ouvir. "Listen to me before you answer."

items.q: "He speaks to the team kindly." Kindly means…
items.why: Kindly = de modo gentil. É o advérbio de "kind".

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem quando falamos de feedback e coaching. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "You are doing well. Keep going!" Keep going means…
items.why: Keep going = continue, siga em frente.

items.q: "Take your time and think. There is no rush." To take your time means to…
options: do it slowly, with no hurry
items.why: Take your time = leve o tempo que precisar, sem pressa.

items.q: "You work fast, but please slow down on the hard parts." Slow down means…
items.why: Slow down = ir mais devagar.

items.q: "That is a good idea. Well done!" We say well done to…
items.why: Well done = parabéns, muito bem — elogio por um bom trabalho.

items.q: "You agreed to do it, so please follow through." Follow through means…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.
